partners.mechanism_chain: DTNBP1 (HGNC:2706) —DISRUPTS→ 22q11.2 deletion syndrome-associated neurodevelopmental defects (HP:0002066); OCRL (HGNC:8117) —DISRUPTS→ PtdIns(4,5)P2 homeostasis (GO:0007259); PtdIns(4,5)P2 homeostasis (GO:0007259) —LEADS_TO→ Oculocerebrorenal syndrome-associated renal anomalies (HP:0000067); PtdIns(4,5)P2 homeostasis (GO:0007259) —LEADS_TO→ Oculocerebrorenal syndrome-associated intellectual disability (HP:0001249); PtdIns(4,5)P2 homeostasis (GO:0007259) —LEADS_TO→ Oculocerebrorenal syndrome-associated eye defects (HP:0000508). While DTNBP1's role in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is complex and involves multiple cellular functions, OCRL is a phosphatase that directly impacts PtdIns(4,5)P2 homeostasis. Dysregulation of PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels due to OCRL deficiency underlies the characteristic renal, ocular, and intellectual disability phenotypes of oculocerebrorenal syndrome. A potential, though less direct, link to DTNBP1 function in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome may involve downstream effects on cellular signaling pathways that are also influenced by phosphoinositide metabolism, suggesting a shared downstream pathway or process disruption.

Dysregulation of PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels due to OCRL deficiency underlies the characteristic renal, ocular, and intellectual disability phenotypes of oculocerebrorenal syndrome.
